status_summary: After the Commission regained a quorum in late 2025, it voted 2-1 on 2026-01-21 to modify the delegation of litigation authority so that every new lawsuit requires Commission approval, and 2-1 on 2026-01-22 to rescind its 2024 harassment enforcement guidance, with the majority arguing it exceeded Title VII. A 2026-01-14 vote, reported by a law firm, gave the Chair control over meeting agendas. A 2026-05-07 EEOC release lists religious freedom, DEI-related discrimination, anti-American bias and women's sex-based rights among its priorities; pregnancy and disability accommodation appear only in individual cases. No disclaimer of consent-decree power or of rulemaking authority was found.

timeline.event: The Commission voted 2-1 on a resolution concerning its authority to commence or intervene in litigation, modifying the long-standing delegation so that new lawsuits proceed only with Commission approval.
The Commission voted 2-1 to rescind its 2024 Enforcement Guidance on Harassment in the Workplace.

title: EEOC governance reforms: Commission votes, guidance rescission, enforcement priorities
uncertainties: The quorum restoration and the 2026-01-14 agenda vote come from law-firm commentary, which gives no exact quorum date; the EEOC votes page for January 2026 lists a 2026-01-13 resolution on Chair and Commission roles in organizational changes but no 2026-01-14 entry, so the two may differ. The votes page lists titles only; the effect of the litigation resolution comes from the law-firm summary. Later months of votes were not reviewed. The 2026-05-07 release is the agency's own characterization of its work and is not treated as an event. The 2026-01-14 vote giving the Chair agenda control runs partly against the Mandate's call to act by majority vote rather than Chair action.
